title: Consumer activation probe
blurb: Canonical installable focus-existing app reading navigator.userActivation.isActive and hasBeenActive synchronously inside launchQueue.setConsumer(), after one task, and after 6 s expiry, alongside tab-side baselines.
question: Does a user-initiated focus-existing launch into an already-open installed web app grant transient navigator.userActivation.isActive inside launchQueue.setConsumer(), and does it expire after 6 seconds?
result: On Chrome for Testing 153 (headless), tab baselines verified load isActive=false, click isActive=true, and +6 s isActive=false with hasBeenActive=true; installed-app launch delivery could not run headless and is not verified in Chrome 160.
testedIn: Chrome for Testing 153 (tab baselines verified); installed-app focus-existing delivery not verified in Chrome 160

friction.summary: LaunchParams does not indicate whether a delivery started a new navigation or reused an existing window
friction.repro: Register launchQueue.setConsumer() in a focus-existing app; both the initial navigating launch (isActive false) and subsequent focus-existing relaunches arrive as indistinguishable LaunchParams objects.
friction.workaround: Check navigator.userActivation.isActive directly inside the consumer rather than trying to infer launch kind, or use a load-time heuristic only for diagnostics.
